content.text: {"origin":"NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, NVIDIA Blog), with partner quotes from Sharon AI's CEO and Firmus's co-CEO as quoted by NVIDIA.","note":"Material source claim: NVIDIA says a new business model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, using a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. Under the partnership, NVIDIA would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which NVIDIA describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. What it supports about the business: NVIDIA is describing a new monetization channel that would add a usage-linked revenue component on top of standard product revenue, and the model includes credit support, which the source does not specify in size, form, or provider. Conditional interpretation: if the program is executed as described, NVIDIA's economics would depend on partner cloud utilization and pricing, and on the size of any credit support it provides. This is a company statement of intent and model design, not a reported result, so it supports a conditional, qualitative view of the business model rather than any quantified revenue. The Firmus Batam campus (expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) and the Sharon AI collaboration are project-stage statements. They are useful as supply-side and demand-side leads for NVIDIA GPUs, but they do not show NVIDIA's direct purchase amounts, contract signing status, or any NVIDIA revenue. The Firmus figures are expectations without a disclosed timeline or financing. Counterexample check: all quoted facts could hold while NVIDIA's share of cloud revenue is small, the credit support is limited or contingent, or the partners' capacity is delayed, so the link from this announcement to material NVIDIA earnings remains a hypothesis that needs the missing terms.","limitations":["The source does not disclose the revenue-share percentage, duration, or how the cloud revenue share is measured for NVIDIA.","The source does not disclose the size, form, provider, or conditions of the credit support in the model, so its financial exposure cannot be assessed.","No signing status is disclosed for any specific AI cloud agreement; the named partners' participation is described as taking shape, not as executed contracts with stated terms.","The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000-GPU figures are expected scale targets with no disclosed completion date, financing, or NVIDIA's share of the purchases.","No NVIDIA financial impact, backlog, or revenue amount from this model is disclosed in the source.","The source is a company blog post with promotional framing; its statements are NVIDIA's own characterization and have not been checked against filings."],"follow_up":["Check NVIDIA's next 10-Q or 10-K for disclosure of revenue-sharing arrangements, cloud revenue share, guarantees, or credit-support commitments tied to AI clouds.","Check whether NVIDIA's filings describe these credit-support arrangements as guarantees, commitments, or contingent liabilities, and how they are measured.","Check Firmus and Sharon AI public filings or announcements for signed agreements with NVIDIA, financing details, and the timing of GPU deployments.","Check whether any named AI cloud partner or NVIDIA-linked credit facility is disclosed with an amount, term, and signing date.","Look for independent reporting or data on the Batam campus construction progress and power contract status to test the expected 360 MW scale."],"proposal":null}
